title: Level 2 Chemistry: Bonding, Structure, Properties and Energy Changes -- 2025
subject: chemistry

questions.text:
Sodium fluoride, NaF, is used as a dietary supplement. In analytical chemistry, it is often reacted with barium chloride, BaCl2, as shown below.

2NaF(aq) + BaCl2(aq) -> BaF2(s) + 2NaCl(aq)

When excess barium chloride, BaCl2, is added to 63.0 g of sodium fluoride, NaF, 72.4 kJ of energy is released.

Calculate the DrH for the above reaction.

M(NaF) = 42.0 g mol-1
questions.expectedAnswer: n(NaF) = 63.0 / 42.0 = 1.500 mol. The equation uses 2 mol NaF per mole of reaction, so n(reaction) = 1.500 / 2 = 0.750 mol. DrH = -72.4 / 0.750 = -96.5 kJ mol-1
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- One step correct.

For Merit:
- Correct answer with unit and negative sign.

questions.text:
Relate the bonding and structure in ionic and molecular solids to their relative melting points.

In your answer:
- describe the bonding and structure in ionic and molecular solids
- explain what the melting point of a solid indicates about the strength of forces between its particles
- link the strength of forces between the particles to their relative melting points.
questions.expectedAnswer: Ionic solids are made of positive and negative ions in a 3D lattice held together by strong ionic bonds. Molecular solids are made of molecules held together by weak intermolecular forces. Higher melting point = stronger forces.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Recognises melting point relates to force strength.

For Merit:
- Describes structure and bonding of ONE solid type and links to melting.

For Excellence:
- Links both solid types to melting point difference.

questions.text:
Boron nitride, BN, and copper, Cu, are both used in technology, but their properties are very different.

Boron nitride is extremely hard and used as an abrasive. Copper is malleable and ductile, and is used to craft fine jewellery and wiring.

Explain how the structure and bonding of each substance results in these properties.

Boron nitride, BN, hardness:

Copper, Cu, malleable and ductile:
questions.expectedAnswer: Boron nitride (in its cubic form) is a 3D covalent network in which every B atom is covalently bonded to 4 N atoms (and vice versa). The strong, directional covalent bonds throughout the entire structure make it very hard. Copper is a metallic solid with a 3D lattice of Cu cations surrounded by delocalised electrons; the non-directional metallic bonds allow layers of cations to slide past each other when a force is applied, without breaking the electrostatic attraction, making copper malleable and ductile.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Recognises that bonding type influences properties.

For Merit:
- Links bonding and structure of ONE solid to properties.

For Excellence:
- Explains both solids.

questions.text:
The Haber process produces ammonia:

N2(g) + 3H2(g) -> 2NH3(g)    DrH = -93.0 kJ mol-1

Calculate the average bond energy of the N-N triple bond in N2, using the average bond energies listed below.

| Bond | Bond energy (kJ mol-1) |
|---|---|
| H-H | 436 |
| N-H | 391 |
questions.expectedAnswer:
Bonds broken: 1 x N-N triple = x, 3 x H-H = 3 x 436 = 1308. Total: 1308 + x.
Bonds formed: 6 x N-H = 6 x 391 = 2346.
DrH = broken - formed: -93.0 = (1308 + x) - 2346. x = 2346 - 1308 - 93.0 = 945 kJ mol-1
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Correctly calculates total bonds broken or formed.

For Merit:
- Correct process with minor error.

For Excellence:
- Correct answer (945 kJ mol-1).

Is the reaction absorbing energy from the surroundings or releasing energy to the surroundings?

Circle the correct option for the enthalpy change of this reaction:

DrH < 0, negative          DrH > 0, positive

All three of the compounds given below contain polar bonds, but only two of them are polar molecules.

| Methanol | Carbon tetrachloride | Hydrogen fluoride |
|---|---|---|
| H-C(H)(H)-OH | Cl-C(Cl)(Cl)-Cl | H-F |

Define what makes a chemical bond polar, and give an example from one of the above compounds.
questions.expectedAnswer: A polar bond is a covalent bond with a permanent dipole, arising because the two atoms have different electronegativities and so share the bonding electrons unequally. Example: the O-H bond in methanol — O is much more electronegative than H, so the bonding electrons spend more time closer to O, giving O a partial negative charge and H a partial positive charge.

questions.text:
Circle the compound that is the non-polar molecule.

Methanol    Carbon tetrachloride    Hydrogen fluoride
Use your understanding of structure and bonding to justify your choice of the non-polar molecule.
questions.expectedAnswer: Carbon tetrachloride has four polar C-Cl bonds arranged symmetrically (tetrahedrally) around the central C atom. Because the four bonds are all equally polar and symmetrically arranged, the individual bond dipoles cancel out exactly, so the molecule has no net dipole moment and is non-polar overall.

WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Identifies symmetry.

For Merit:

For Excellence:
- Full explanation.

questions.text:
What makes potassium iodide, KI, soluble in water, but iodine, I2, insoluble in water?

In your answer:
- refer to the structure and bonding of each substance
- explain how the substance interacts with water molecules
- include a diagram showing the dissolving of KI in water.
questions.expectedAnswer: KI is ionic — it has a 3D lattice of K+ and I- ions held together by strong ionic bonds. Polar water molecules attract the ions: the partial negative O ends of water attract K+ and the partial positive H ends attract I-. These ion-dipole attractions are strong enough to overcome the ionic lattice, so KI dissolves. I2 is a non-polar molecular solid held together by weak dispersion forces. Water molecules form stronger hydrogen bonds with each other than they can form with I2, so I2 does not dissolve in water and remains insoluble.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Identifies attractions needed.

For Merit:
- Links forces to solubility for ONE compound.

For Excellence:
- Explains both with diagram.

questions.text:
Different allotropes of carbon have different electrical conductivities. Diamond does not conduct, but graphite does.

Compare and contrast the structure and bonding of diamond and graphite.

In your answer:
- explain the structure and bonding of each
- define electrical conductivity in solids
- justify the difference in conductivity.
questions.expectedAnswer: Diamond: each C bonded to 4 others in 3D network, no free electrons. Graphite: each C bonded to 3 others in layers with delocalised electrons that can carry charge.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Describes diamond OR graphite structure.

For Merit:
- Explains both and links conductivity to delocalised electrons.

For Excellence:
- Comprehensive explanation.

questions.text:
Calculate the energy change when 168 g of calcium oxide, CaO, is produced.

2Ca(s) + O2(g) -> 2CaO(s)    DrH = -1270 kJ mol-1

M(CaO) = 56.1 g mol-1
questions.expectedAnswer: n(CaO) = 168 / 56.1 = 2.995 mol. The equation produces 2 mol CaO per -1270 kJ, so energy per mole of CaO = -1270 / 2 = -635 kJ mol-1. Energy change = 2.995 x (-635) = -1902 kJ (1902 kJ of energy released).

questions.text:
Draw the Lewis structure for each molecule and give their shapes.

| Molecule | NO2 | SF2 | BF3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lewis structure | | | |
| Name of shape | | | |
questions.expectedAnswer: NO2: bent (the central N has one unpaired electron / single electron plus two bonding regions to oxygen, giving a bent shape). SF2: bent (the central S atom has two bonding pairs and two lone pairs, giving a bent shape). BF3: trigonal planar (the central B atom has three bonding pairs and no lone pairs).

questions.text:
Compare the shapes and bond angles of germane (GeH4) and arsine (AsH3).

| | Germane (GeH4) | Arsine (AsH3) |
|---|---|---|
| Shape | tetrahedral | trigonal pyramidal |
| Bond angle | 109.5 degrees | 92 degrees |

Compare the two shapes and explain the factors that contribute to:
- arrangement around the central atom
- molecular shape.
questions.expectedAnswer: In germane (GeH4), the central Ge atom has four bonding regions and no lone pairs, so the four Ge-H bonding pairs repel one another equally and arrange themselves tetrahedrally at 109.5 degrees. In arsine (AsH3), the central As atom has four regions of electron density (three As-H bonding pairs plus one lone pair), giving an overall tetrahedral arrangement of electron density but a trigonal pyramidal molecular shape (ignoring the lone pair). The lone pair repels the bonding pairs more strongly than bonding pairs repel each other, compressing the H-As-H bond angles below 109.5 degrees.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Identifies correct electron regions.

For Merit:
- Links electron regions and lone pairs to shape for ONE compound.

For Excellence:
- Fully explains both.
